_note: Illustrative sample data. Species facts, features and conservation tags must be checked against DFO / SARA before the demo.

species.name: Copper rockfish
features: Spiny dorsal fin running along the back
Pale stripe along the rear half of the side
Large head and mouth with a deep body
species.blurb: One of the most common rockfish at ONC's BC coastal cameras. Rockfish live for decades, so changes in how often they're seen can be an early conservation signal.
species.habitatHint: Rocky reefs, often resting on the bottom near cover.
species.modelNote: Hotspot positions are in scene units (model root is scaled 0.35 and shifted).

species.name: Quillback rockfish
features: Very tall, deeply notched spiny dorsal fin
Dark brown body with yellow-orange speckles on the head
Pale area in front of the dorsal fin
species.blurb: Listed as Threatened. Hard to tell from copper rockfish in murky footage, which is why people check these clips.
species.habitatHint: Rocky reefs and boulder fields, close to the bottom.

species.name: Lingcod
features: Very large mouth with visible teeth
Long, continuous dorsal fin with a notch in the middle
species.blurb: A large predator of rocky reefs. Often seen lying still on the bottom near rockfish.
species.habitatHint: Rocky bottoms, often motionless near crevices.

species.name: Kelp greenling
features: Slender body with a single long dorsal fin
species.blurb: A common reef fish in shallow BC waters. Its colour varies a lot between males and females.
